> **What this case shows** — the AR fit gave coefficients; its **payoff is a spectrum**. The
> **AR (parametric) spectral density** turns a handful of coefficients into a smooth, sharp-peaked PSD —
> the parametric alternative to the periodogram. This case adds it (**`arSpectrum`**), completing the
> time-series lane. On a real eyes-closed EEG channel it reproduces **`stats::spec.ar`** **bit-for-bit**
> (max |rel diff| ~**5e-14**), and its peak (**10.9 Hz**) lands in the **alpha band** and agrees within
> **~0.5 Hz** with the nonparametric periodogram peak — two spectral estimators, one verdict.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — `arSpectrum(x, order, n_freq)` → the parametric AR spectral density over frequency.
**Way of thinking** — a periodogram spends one parameter per frequency; an AR spectrum spends `order`
parameters total and interpolates the rest. That makes it smooth and low-variance — ideal for a clean
resonant peak — but it can only show as much structure as its order allows. Read it alongside the
periodogram: agreement is confidence, divergence is a hint to raise the order.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioAnalysis::arSpectrum()`, built on `arYuleWalker()`.
:::

## Proposition

On real eyes-closed POz EEG, `arSpectrum` reproduces `stats::spec.ar` bit-for-bit (max |rel diff|
~5e-14); its peak (10.9 Hz) is in the alpha band and agrees within ~0.5 Hz with the smoothed-periodogram
peak (11.4 Hz).

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and a cross-check: having fit the AR model, can we author its parametric
spectrum, reproduce base-R spec.ar exactly, and confirm its alpha peak agrees with the nonparametric
periodogram?** The goal is to introduce `arSpectrum`, certify it bit-for-bit, and read the cross-method
agreement.

## Challenge & approach

The AR spectral density is S(f) = σ²/|1 − Σ φ_k e^{−i2πf k}|², from a Yule-Walker AR(order) fit
(`arYuleWalker`), evaluated on n_freq frequencies in [0, 0.5]. We compute the AR(8) spectrum and check
it against `stats::spec.ar`, then compare its peak to `stats::spec.pgram` (smoothed periodogram).

```
EEG POz (eegmmidb) → AR(8) Yule-Walker → S(f) = var / |1 - sum phi_k e^{-i2pi f k}|^2  (500 freqs)
                    vs stats::spec.ar → bit-exact (~5e-14, incl. N/(N-p-1) variance)
                    AR peak 10.9 Hz  ~=  periodogram peak 11.4 Hz  (alpha; parametric vs nonparametric)
```

## Data

**EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb, PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, run **R02
(eyes-closed)**, channel **POz**, 10 s at 160 Hz — the same git-tracked vector the
[autocorrelation](../autocorrelation-eegmmidb/index.qmd), [PACF](../pacf-eegmmidb/index.qmd) and
[AR](../ar-yule-walker-eegmmidb/index.qmd) cases use. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

agreeing on the alpha peak); the right panel is the certification against base-R spec.ar.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| **AR spectrum peak** | **10.9 Hz** (alpha) |
| op vs `stats::spec.ar` (max \|rel diff\|) | **5e-14** (bit-exact) |
| frequency bins | **500** |
| peak in alpha band (8-13 Hz) | **yes** |
| smoothed-periodogram peak | **11.4 Hz** |
| \|AR − periodogram\| peak difference | **0.5 Hz** |

The newly-authored op equals spec.ar at every frequency, and its alpha peak matches the periodogram.
Values trace to [`artifacts/arspec_summary.csv`](artifacts/arspec_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`arSpectrum` completes the ACF → PACF → AR → tests lane with the AR model's spectral payoff, and it is
exact: bit-for-bit against `stats::spec.ar`. The transferable takeaway: **the AR spectrum and the
periodogram are two lenses on the same power. The AR lens is smooth and cheap — perfect for a clean
resonant peak like alpha — and when it agrees with the periodogram (as here, within 0.5 Hz), you can
trust the peak; when it doesn't, raise the order or reach for the nonparametric estimate.**

## Open questions

- The AR order controls smoothness (too low blurs peaks, too high adds spurious ones); AIC/BIC selection
  over `arYuleWalker` fits would make `arSpectrum` self-tuning, and comparing the AR peak's bandwidth to
  the periodogram's would quantify the resolution/variance trade-off. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| AR parametric spectrum | `arSpectrum()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| AR fit (coefficients) | `arYuleWalker()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| AR order (PACF cut-off) | `partialAutocorrelation()` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **order** — the AR order (default 8); higher orders resolve more peaks but risk spurious ones. Pick it
  from the PACF cut-off or by AIC/BIC.
- **n_freq** — the number of frequency bins in [0, 0.5] (default 500); the AR spectrum is smooth, so a
  moderate grid suffices.
- **convention** — matches `stats::spec.ar` (the small-sample innovation variance N/(N−p−1)); multiply by
  the sampling rate to place the frequency axis in Hz.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioAnalysis)

s <- arSpectrum(x, order = 8, n_freq = 500)
s$freq[which.max(s$spec)] * 160   # peak frequency in Hz (sampling rate 160)
# reproduces stats::spec.ar bit-for-bit; the peak agrees with the periodogram.
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/arspec_summary.csv`](artifacts/arspec_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the
AR peak frequency, the bit-exact spec.ar match, the alpha-band peak, the periodogram peak and their
cross-method difference, and the honestly-noted scope (newly-authored op building on arYuleWalker;
machine-precision incl. the spec.ar variance convention; parametric/nonparametric agreement).
